MANDATORY, per ISS-0768's own acceptance criteria (docs/issues/ISS-0768.yaml) -- investigate and RECORD whether this is a regression or has been broken since RoleRegistry shipped. This is not optional and not a formality -- ORCH will check your result names a specific SHA-backed finding, not a restatement of the design doc's instructions.

Run mix compile --warnings-as-errors and the full mix test suite (at minimum test/letflow/identity/role_registry_test.exs and any test/letflow/routers/identity_test.exs) and quote real output in your result -- never a prediction. Do not write the NEW cross-tenant-isolation regression test yourself -- that is TEST-DESIGNER's job at step-05; you are only responsible for making the EXISTING suite compile and pass against the new arities.

Branch feature/WF03-ISS0768-20260921 is checked out in this worktree (c:\Users\tvolo\dev\ai-dala\letflow-wf03-iss0768) -- work there, do not touch c:\Users\tvolo\dev\ai-dala\letflow (a different concurrent session owns uncommitted work there on an unrelated issue). result.summary:
Implemented exactly per lib/letflow/design/iss0768-role-registry-tenant-prefix.md: role_registry.ex now has list_roles/1, upsert_role/3, do_upsert_role/3 (private), insert_or_update_role/3 (private), each threading opts :: [prefix: String.t()] into their Repo call (Repo.all/2, Repo.transaction/2 with prefix on the transaction call itself plus explicit prefix: on the inner Repo.get/3 and Repo.insert/2 too, per the design's defense-in-depth instruction). resolve_role_in_tx/1 is byte-for-byte unchanged (confirmed: `git diff` on role_registry.ex shows zero touched lines in that function). routers/identity.ex: handle_list_roles/2 and handle_upsert_role/2 now take opts as a second param, and the route macro bodies for GET/POST /roles pass conn.assigns.scoped_opts, matching every other route in the module (e.g. handle_create(conn, conn.assigns.scoped_opts) at line 143).

REGRESSION-VS-ALWAYS-BROKEN FINDING (ran exactly the design section-4 commands against this worktree's real history): `git log -p --follow -S"prefix" -- lib/letflow/identity/role_registry.ex` returned a COMPLETELY EMPTY result -- no commit in this file's history has ever added or removed a line containing the string 'prefix'. Corroborating check: `git log --follow --diff-filter=A --format=%H -- lib/letflow/identity/role_registry.ex` names the file's sole introduction commit as a1c4ab9b7d61c852c612ed03a51a64cbf52d1371 ('feat: Per-tenant role registry (TenantRoleStore/IDN-05 equivalent) [WF02-REQ020-20260816] (#40)'); `git show a1c4ab9b7d61c852c612ed03a51a64cbf52d1371 -- lib/letflow/identity/role_registry.ex | grep prefix` matched nothing. The file's entire commit history is exactly two commits (`git log --follow --oneline`): a1c4ab9b (introduction) and d894d1f6 ('fix(REQ-251): apply .zig provenance-marking convention -- identity.ex + identity/* + oidc/* (#983)', a comment/provenance-only edit). CONCLUSION: this is NOT a regression -- Letflow.Identity.RoleRegistry has issued unprefixed (default-schema) queries since it first shipped under REQ-020; ISS-0768 is fixing a bug that has existed since the module's introduction, not something a later commit broke.
